task: Run a retrospective on the PR #4290 suppression decision, then correct that retrospective after discovering its premise was false. PR #4302 did not falsify the #4290 rationale; the repository owner closed #4302 as the wrong fix and stated the suppression's rationale is correct on the merits.

events.content: Measured taste_count_ratchet.py against a clean origin/main worktree at ede9fd1fe and got OK at baseline 601, exit 0, which showed main was not red.
Read PR #4302's diff and wrongly concluded it falsified the PR #4290 suppression rationale, then wrote a retrospective and an always-on rule change on that premise.
Surveyed PR state and found #4302 CLOSED, with the author stating it is the wrong fix and that the suppression's rationale is correct on the merits.
Found that the ratchet memory's split-not-suppress guidance is scoped to test files, so quoting it for a registration module stripped the population it was measured on.
Reverted the rule change and both regenerated instruction mirrors, and confirmed instruction_budget.py independently rejects the addition at 83100 of 83000 bytes.
Rewrote the retrospective to record the real failure, which is that a self-blaming conclusion skipped the evidence bar applied to every other conclusion.
